messages:
maria_g: :rotating_light: getting alerts — api-gateway -> smart-router shows a spike in 5xxs starting ~2:34 UTC. latency also up for gen endpoints. dashboards show heavy traffic to us-west-2 and a lot of fallbacks to cpu-quantized-1 variant.
liam_b: looking. are those client retries causing extra load? any cc on retry headers?
conor_dev: noticed a policy change deployed ~2:20 that added automatic region-fallback + aggressive retry routing for multi-region. could be misrouting to the wrong variant under capacity pressure.
maria_g: customer impact: ~12% error rate on /v1/generate for a subset of enterprise tenants, latency p95 up 4x. a few customers reported timeouts and reconnects.
incident-bot: Pager duty: page sent to SRE oncall. Incident severity: SEV2. Pager: @sre-oncall
sre-oncall: on it. taking lead. @conor_dev can you paste the routing policy diff? also which variants are considered compatible for fallback?
conor_dev: paste below:

```
- smart_routing:
-   prefer_region: us-east-1
-   fallback_order: [us-east-1, us-west-2]
-   variant_policy:
-     compatible_variants: [gpu-base, cpu-quantized-1]
-     prefer_cheaper: true
+ smart_routing:
+   prefer_region: us-east-1
+   fallback_order: [us-west-2, us-east-1]
+   variant_policy:
+     compatible_variants: [cpu-quantized-1, gpu-base]
+     prefer_cheaper: true
```
conor_dev: tl;dr: fallback_order got flipped and compatible_variants prioritized cpu-quantized-1. that was an accidental merge from the cost-ops change.
liam_b: ah — so under load the router sends to us-west-2 cpu-quantized-1 which saturates and then triggers more fallbacks -> circular. clients retrying immediately double the traffic back into the loop.
maria_g: we are seeing amplification: client avg retries=3, many without jitter. requests -> fallback -> increased latency -> client retries -> more fallbacks. classic thundering herd.
jen_prodops: immediate customer mitigation options?
sre-oncall: short-term plan:
1) disable the faulty fallback policy (set `smart_routing.fallback_enabled=false`) to stop cross-region fallback.
2) apply a regional cap: `regional_cap: 0.7` on us-west-2 so it won't accept >70% of fallback traffic.
3) set server-side retry-suppression header for responses from fallback targets: `X-Redwood-Retry-Suppress: true` so SDKs/clients can reduce retries.
conor_dev: I'm pushing a hotfix now to roll back the fallback_order and deprioritize cpu variants for these customers. deploying to edge config.
deploy-bot: deploy started for config hotfix (cfg-rollback-218776). rolling to control-plane in stages.
liam_b: also ask client SDK team to push a minor patch to add exponential backoff + jitter and cap retries to 2 for affected tenants. I'll ping them.
jen_prodops: contacting top 5 affected customers with known mitigation steps & status note. drafting incident banner for status.redwood.ai
maria_g: quick mitigation commands I'm running now:
```
# disable fallback
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://control.redwood/api/v1/configs/smart_routing -d '{"fallback_enabled": false}'

# set regional cap
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://control.redwood/api/v1/traffic_caps -d '{"region":"us-west-2","cap":0.7}'
```
sre-oncall: made both changes. monitoring metrics now. can people watch error-rate and token per-second on us-east-1 and us-west-2?
liam_b: watching. error-rate trending down after config change. p95 latency drifting down but still elevated for some sessions.
conor_dev: hotfix config deployed and verified. router logs show fewer cross-region handoffs.
maria_g: good. still seeing bursts from one tenant who has no jitter. we need to throttle at edge for that customer.
sre-oncall: applied soft throttle on tenant: tenant_rate_limit=0.5 (half normal) for 10m window. also enabled `circuit_breaker` for cpu-quantized-1 variant to fail-fast.
jen_prodops: customer comms: initial message sent, offering temporary opt-out for fallback and priority queueing. legal and support looped in.
liam_b: confirm: are any models in the catalog mismarked as "compatible" when they actually have different latency/throughput profiles? we should add metadata to avoid CPU variants being auto-preferred.
conor_dev: yeah, we should tighten compatible_variant matching to include a perf profile and sequence-length budget. opening a ticket: RNW-3642.
maria_g: SLO check — SLA blips for affected customers. ops will prepare crediting calc.
incident-bot: oncall handoff reminder: if this spans >2 hours escalate to SEV1. current elapsed: 18m.
sre-oncall: handoff to liam_b in 40m if stable. next steps for postmortem:
- root cause: bad merge flipped fallback/variant prioritization
- contributing: client SDK retries without jitter + no server-side retry suppression
- mitigation enacted: rollback fallback_order, disable fallback, regional cap, tenant throttle, circuit breaker, SDK patch request
- follow-ups: RNW-3642 (variant perf metadata), RNW-3643 (server header to discourage retries), RNW-3644 (routing policy CI to prevent regressions), RNW-3645 (customer retry guidance in SDK docs)
maria_g: adding timeline logs and sample router traces to the thread. will attach in postmortem doc.
liam_b: worth noting: short-term we should add a server-side token-bucket to reject excessive retries earlier. I'll prototype.
conor_dev: thanks team — I'll own the rollback PR and RNW tasks. leave the incident open until error-rate normalizes to baseline for 30m.
jen_prodops: continuing comms. support to flag any customers who need SLA credits.
sre-oncall: monitoring. will update in 10m or sooner if anything changes. thumbs up if you are on this thread: :thumbsup:
maria_g: :thumbsup:
liam_b: :thumbsup:
conor_dev: :thumbsup:
jen_prodops: :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated; next update scheduled in 10m."
